sprint: Root README Template and Update Workflow Sprint

q1_reusable_sections.answer: The following README sections are structurally reusable across families: title block with badges, Overview, Included Examples, Requirements, How to Run, Package Installation, Validation Status, Repository Layout, Useful Links, License/Support.
q1_reusable_sections.note: All content must be template-parameterized. No static family-specific text in the template.

q2_parameterized_sections.answer: All sections must be parameterized. Specific parameters by section:
q2_parameterized_sections.title: display_name (e.g. Aspose.Cells for .NET)
q2_parameterized_sections.badges: nuget_package_id for NuGet URLs; target_repo_owner/target_repo_name for GitHub badge
q2_parameterized_sections.overview: display_name, product_name, api_description derived from family
q2_parameterized_sections.included_examples_table: examples list (name, type, input_format, output_format, run_command) from package discovery
q2_parameterized_sections.how_to_run: family name for example path prefix
q2_parameterized_sections.useful_links: nuget_url, product_page_url, docs_url, api_reference_url, blog_url, support_url, temporary_license_url — all family-specific

q5_lowcode_adaptations.answer: The README must describe LowCode-specific API classes, not the full Aspose product suite. Key adaptations required:
points: Overview must describe LowCode namespace and what 'one-line' processing means in context of this family
Examples table must list only the 4 or 9 LowCode API classes (HtmlConverter, ImageConverter, etc.), not all Aspose classes
No references to full Aspose product features (mail merge, chart rendering, etc.)
No references to DocFX or API documentation for non-LowCode classes
Allowed types for Words must note the controlled pilot scope (Converter, Watermarker, Splitter, Replacer)
Run commands must use actual example directory names from the package

q6_integration_point.timing: After example_dirs is resolved from package_path, before build_pr() and create_github_pr() are called
q6_integration_point.scope: Both dry-run and live publish — README must be in every package
q6_integration_point.secondary: render-root-readme CLI command for standalone preview without publish
q6_integration_point.note: github_pr_publisher.py already uploads all files from package_path not in _EXCLUDED_FILENAMES. README.md is not excluded. No changes to github_pr_publisher.py needed.

jinja2_missing.resolution: Add Jinja2>=3.1 to [project] dependencies; run pip install -e .
jinja2_missing.severity: BLOCKING — must be resolved before Phase 2

templates_dir_missing.resolution: Create with mkdir; template file is created in Phase 1
templates_dir_missing.severity: MINOR — not blocking, created in Phase 1

readme_not_in_existing_packages.observation: Neither cells-controlled-pilot nor words-controlled-pilot contains README.md
readme_not_in_existing_packages.resolution: README.md is generated and written by the renderer during this sprint — no backfill of merged remote repos needed

design_decisions.template_engine: Jinja2 — standard Python template engine, full for-loop and variable support for Examples table
design_decisions.new_yaml_fields: none — all context derived from existing family config + evidence files
design_decisions.integration_location: publish-pr handler in __main__.py (not inside publisher.py::publish_examples), to also work for dry-run path which returns early
design_decisions.readme_in_package_root: README.md at package_path/README.md; github_pr_publisher.py picks it up automatically
design_decisions.audit_blocks_packaging: README audit failure blocks package step to prevent publishing stale or broken READMEs
design_decisions.exit_code: render-root-readme exits 0 on pass, non-zero if required metadata missing or audit fails
